light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

clips.text: Tercera pregunta: ¿cuándo se puede pisar? Y no te voy a inventar una hora exacta, porque depende del calor y del cemento.
clips.action: He holds up three fingers, then shrugs honestly with both palms up, glancing at the sky.

clips.text: La regla es esta: no se pisa hasta que esté duro, y se mantiene húmedo varios días. El envase de tu cemento te dice los tiempos.
clips.action: He presses his thumb against the new grooved floor as he crouches, then stands and mimes spraying water with his hand.

clips.text: Y la cuarta, que me encanta: ¿la escoba no lo deja rayado? Sí. Justamente. Ese rayado es para que no resbales cuando llueve.
clips.action: He grabs the patio broom leaning on the porch post, turns it bristles up and grins, then points down at the grooves on the floor.

clips.text: Adentro de la casa, en una habitación, no se usa escoba: se alisa con la llana. Afuera, en el patio, el rayado es lo que te cuida.
clips.action: He points toward the back door of the house, makes a smooth flat gliding gesture with his hand, then points down at the grooved patio floor.

clips.text: ¿Y con rodillo? No. Esto no es una pintura. Una pintura de cemento es finita, y lo finito es justo lo que se despega.
clips.action: He mimes rolling a paint roller up and down in the air, then shakes his head and wags a finger.

clips.text: ¿Y sobre tierra? Tampoco. Sobre tierra primero va un contrapiso, que es otro trabajo. Esto es para renovar un piso que ya existe.
clips.action: He points down past the patio as if at bare earth, shakes his head, then taps the floor with the broom handle.

clips.text: ¿Y cuánto dura? Depende de cómo lo hagas y de lo que le pase por encima. Pero bien hecho, es un piso de cemento.
clips.action: He leans the broom back against the post, stamps once on the new floor, then opens his hands.

clips.text: No es una pintura que se gasta en un año: es una capa de verdad, pegada a la de abajo. Por eso los pasos importan tanto.
clips.action: He holds his thumb and index finger very close together as if showing something thin, shakes his head, then spreads them wider.

clips.text: ¿Y la escoba? Una de patio, de cerdas duras de plástico. Nueva, o bien lavada. No la de barrer la cocina, que es blandita.
clips.action: He holds up the patio broom and runs his gloveless fingers through its stiff bristles, then pretends to sweep gently like a kitchen broom and laughs.
